explanation:
[EFFECT] Higher wind speed consistently reduces predicted bike demand, with a roughly monotonic downward effect. At calm conditions (near zero wind), the model's contribution from wind speed is close to neutral or very slightly positive. As wind speed increases beyond about 20 km/h (normalised value ~0.3), the contribution becomes increasingly negative, dragging predicted demand down. At very high winds (~40–57 km/h, normalised ≥0.5), the effect becomes strongly negative, multiplying predicted demand down by a large factor.

[IMPORTANCE] Wind speed is the **second-least important** feature in the model, ranked 8th out of 9, with a global importance score of 0.020 — roughly 40 times smaller than the top feature (hour of day) and about a quarter of the next-weakest feature (humidity). It plays a minor but real suppressive role at high wind speeds.

[RECOMMENDATION] Since high winds meaningfully suppress demand, consider reducing bike redistribution efforts and staffing levels on forecasted high-wind days (especially above ~20–25 km/h), directing those resources to calmer days when demand is more likely to be at full potential.
